For electric buses, SCF declines from 0.76 (2030) to 0.59 (2040), and other vehicle groups show similarly decreasing trends across the horizon. These SCF estimates provide practical inputs for grid-aware charging infrastructure planning, including diversity factors for sizing distribution transformers and feeders, identifying peak-hour stress, and informing demand management measures such as time of use tariffs and basic smart charging controls.

papers.title: Formalizing inverse problems in the age of AI: possibilities, pitfalls, and an invitation
papers.abstract: Proof assistants such as Lean check mathematical proofs down to the axioms, and AI agents have recently made writing such proofs cheap. We describe AutoIP, a Lean library in which classical linear regularization theory, together with the functional analysis it rests on, has been autoformalized by AI agents. A machine-checked proof certifies only the formal statement it proves, so the remaining human task is to confirm that each formal statement says what was intended. We organize the library around this task: a reviewer compares the formal statements with their natural-language counterparts and never needs to read a proof. Our experience is that the risks lie in the statements rather than in the proofs, and that simple automated tests on the statements can expose problems even in the established literature. We illustrate this with a textbook theorem whose hypothesis is more restrictive than asserted. We invite the inverse problems community to extend and build on the library.

papers.title: Multi-Period Bilevel Coordination of Primary and Secondary Frequency Regulation for Grid-Forming Battery Energy Storage
papers.abstract: We study the coordination of primary and secondary frequency regulation by grid-forming battery energy storage systems in islanded microgrids. We formulate the coordination as a multi-period bilevel program, in which the upper level schedules secondary regulation setpoints and each lower level computes primary regulation decisions. Using the lower-level Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions, we obtain an exact single-level reformulation with complementarity constraints. To address the numerical difficulties introduced by these constraints, we develop a continuation method that couples the complementarity relaxation parameter with the interior-point barrier parameter and warm-starts successive stages. Under the stated boundedness assumptions and with vanishing subproblem residuals, we prove that every accumulation point is feasible and satisfies a first-order stationarity condition for the reformulated problem (C-stationarity). Numerical results for an islanded microgrid show that the proposed method reduces solution time by 89.3% and peak frequency deviation by 0.53% relative to conventional Scholtes relaxation.

papers.title: SafeStart: Mitigating the Overlooked Safety Cost of Active Expert Reduction in MoE LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models send each token through a few of many expert subnetworks. Serving methods make these models faster by running even fewer experts per token, and they are validated on accuracy benchmarks. We show that these methods can weaken the model's refusal of harmful requests, and we introduce SafeStart, which largely restores refusal while keeping most of the speedup. In vLLM on one RTX A6000, keeping about two thirds of the selected experts speeds up offline decoding by 15 to 28% at batch size 8. We find that, at this setting, under a jailbreak that tells the model not to refuse, the share of harmful requests that the model answers rises by 18.4 percentage points on Qwen1.5-MoE, 9.5 on OLMoE, and 6.6 on DeepSeek-V2-Lite, the three of nine models where it rises significantly, while MMLU accuracy drops by less than two points. We discover that most of this increase arises while the model processes the prompt and generates its first few tokens. SafeStart therefore runs all experts for the prompt and the first eight generated tokens, and the reduced set of experts afterwards, through a fused kernel in vLLM. With experts removed, SafeStart keeps at least 85% of the offline decode speedup at batch sizes 8 and 32 and brings the change under this jailbreak to between -2.1 and +1.3 points for three expert-reduction methods on these three models. On 889 held-out requests, in an analysis fixed before generation, truncation raises harmful compliance by 5.8 to 21.4 points, and SafeStart leaves a rise of 0.6 to 2.6 points, non-inferior to the original model on two of the three models. Our results show that faster MoE serving need not cost safety: a serving system can keep most of the gain from running fewer experts by running all of them at the start of each response, and it should test refusal, not only accuracy, before it enables such a method.

papers.title: Hadamard configurations and sharp cubic-period bounds for stealth in dimensions 10, 11, and 12
papers.abstract: We construct explicit, nonlattice periodic point configurations in dimensions $10$, $11$ and $12$ with stealth center density $1/24$ and unit-density stealth radius $2\cdot24^{-1/n}$. These values exceed those of duals of the current record lattice packings, without claiming to exceed all possible lattices. The construction uses the $24$ sign rows of an order-$12$ Hadamard matrix and their antipodes, projected onto $n$ coordinates. For an arbitrary, not necessarily binary, equally weighted motif with marked period $2\mathbb{Z}^n$, we prove a sharp $2n$-point lower bound for a raw stealth radius at least one and classify equality by antipodal Hadamard configurations. We deduce bounded-complexity optimality, sharp optimality among binary motifs in dimensions $10$--$12$, and local maximality under simultaneous perturbations of the motif and the marked period shape. A divisibility argument excludes ordinary equally weighted periodic formal duals. Statements are confined to their indicated classes; no global optimality among arbitrary-period configurations is asserted.

papers.title: Grounding in the Dark: Text-Only Training for Zero-Shot Video Temporal Localization
papers.abstract: Video-LLMs are typically trained on paired video-text data for temporal tasks, yet collecting precise temporal annotations and training on large-scale video datasets are both costly. We investigate whether a text-only LLM, with no vision-language pretraining, can be trained on textual video descriptions alone to perform temporal grounding and receive video only at inference time. This setting removes paired video data from training altogether and is a step toward training multimodal models without paired annotations. We generate a 134K-example corpus of textual sequences with up to 100 time steps, adapt Qwen3-8B with LoRA on CLIP or LLM2CLIP text embeddings, and evaluate on Charades-STA and QV-Highlights without training on videos from either benchmark. LLM2CLIP, whose text encoder supports longer inputs, represents detailed descriptions better than CLIP (61.54 versus 53.86 mtIoU on Temporal-TextVid) and transfers them better to video. Still, replacing text with frame embeddings at inference yields only 4.99 mtIoU on Charades-STA and 11.12 on QV-Highlights, revealing a large modality gap. To bridge it, we propose Nearest Entity Replacement (NER), a training-free mapping that represents each video frame by the normalized mean of its nearest text-entity embeddings, so that the model receives the kind of input it was trained on. NER reaches 14.45 mtIoU on Charades-STA and 20.72 on QV-Highlights, outperforming the strongest of four families of modality-gap baselines by 5.00 and 1.71 points. NER thus enables partial transfer from text to video, while more reliable grounding will likely require encoders with better-aligned text and visual representations.

papers.title: Aperture-dependent [O III] profile variability: Clues to the nature of double-peaked narrow emission lines
papers.abstract: We propose a simple and practical aperture-dependent method for investigating the physical origin of double-peaked narrow emission lines (DPNELs). Spectroscopic observations obtained from different apertures probe different spatial regions and therefore different gas kinematics within the narrow line region (NLR). Consequently, changes in the profiles of DPNELs observed with different apertures can provide important constraints on their physical origins. We applied this method to SDSS J0941 by comparing spectra obtained from the SDSS, DESI, and LAMOST surveys. Significant differences are found in the double-peaked profiles of the different spectra, demonstrating that aperture effects can strongly influence the integrated DPNEL profiles. The AGN model, where the two nuclei lie in a plane perpendicular to the line of sight, can qualitatively explain the asymmetric sampling of the two NLRs, but it cannot explain the different peak separations of different spectra. The observed asymmetric evolution of the two components disfavors a simple AGN-driven outflow and a rotating disk-like NLR scenario. Of the models considered, only a more complex non-axisymmetric rotating NLR provides a self-consistent explanation for the observed aperture-dependent variations. In this scenario, the blueshifted emitting region is more compact and remains largely enclosed by the smaller aperture, resulting in an increased line width with little change in flux. In contrast, the redshifted emitting region is more spatially extended and is therefore more strongly affected by the reduced aperture, leading to pronounced decreases in both flux and line width. Our results illustrate the diagnostic potential of combining multi-aperture spectroscopic surveys to study DPNEL origins, while highlighting the difficulty of distinguishing between physical scenarios.

papers.title: CARM: Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking for Reliable Scientific Super-Resolution
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based super-resolution (SR) can reconstruct fine-scale Earth-observation fields from coarse observations, but reconstruction accuracy alone does not provide a calibrated rule for identifying reliable spatial regions. Conformal Mask Calibration (CMC), built on conformal risk control, converts a spatial uncertainty score into a trust mask and controls the expected worst-case local distortion under exchangeability. However, its fixed threshold can become miscalibrated in Earth-observation streams affected by seasonality and episodic events. We propose $\textit{CARM}$ (Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking), a statistical framework for adaptive spatial risk control under temporal distribution shift. CARM maintains experts with heterogeneous update rates and aggregates their threshold proposals online using an asymmetric surrogate loss, balancing rapid adaptation to distribution changes against stability during relatively stationary periods. All updates are causal and use only mature feedback available after a fixed delay, allowing CARM to operate with any SR model that provides a spatial uncertainty score. We prove that the time-averaged mask-conditioned risk converges to at most $α$ at an $O(1/T)$ rate, without distributional assumptions and for any choice of aggregation weights across experts. On a daily South China Sea chlorophyll-$\textit{a}$ SR stream, CARM reduces the empirical violation rate from $43.49\%$ to $9.38\%$ and the moving-average exceedance frequency from $47.29\%$ to $1.22\%$ at $α=0.10$, while retaining a non-trivial trusted region. Experiments on ERA5 wind and OSTIA sea-surface temperature further show consistent relative improvements across multiple SR backbones.

papers.title: Pushing the frontiers of low-frequency radio astronomy: An ultra-deep sub-arcsecond LOFAR image of ELAIS-N1
papers.abstract: We present ultra-deep sub-arcsecond radio images of the ELAIS-N1 field covering 2.5x2.5 deg^2, produced from 200 hours of LOw Frequency ARray (LOFAR) observations in the 115-168 MHz band. The radio continuum images are obtained using recent advances in LOFAR long-baseline calibration and imaging. We achieve a central point-source sensitivity of 5.3 $μ$Jy/beam at an angular resolution of 0.33"x0.39" and an area-weighted sensitivity of 7.4 $μ$Jy/beam at 0.36"x0.45", making these the deepest radio images below 1.28 GHz to date and among the deepest at any radio frequency. By combining our data with previously released deep 6" LOFAR images, we compile a catalogue with a total of 62,916 unique radio sources across 2.5x2.5 deg^2. Our calibration strategy, combined with astrometric alignment using 95 Gaia quasars, results in positional offsets of $Δ$RA = -3 $\pm$ 27 mas and $Δ$DEC = 2 $\pm$ 17 mas for these same sources. We further demonstrate the potential for deep polarisation studies at sub-arcsecond resolution with instrumental leakages from Stokes I into linear polarisation down to 0.12%, which is about a factor of two better than the typical leakage in the LOFAR Two-metre Sky Survey at 6" resolution. Our results demonstrate that imaging a large number of observations over a wide field area at sub-arcsecond resolution is now computationally feasible. This establishes a new benchmark for low-frequency radio imaging in terms of combining depth, resolution, and survey area, which lays the foundation for deeper and wider surveys in the LOFAR2.0 and SKA era.
authors: J. M. G. H. J. de Jong

papers.title: Flux-Matched Poisson Iteration for Generated Jacobian Equations: Local Convergence and Spectral Galerkin Approximation
papers.abstract: We develop a flux-matched Poisson iteration for solving generated Jacobian equations with second boundary conditions. In each step, it solves a fixed shifted Poisson problem with a Neumann-type boundary condition. Near a smooth regular solution with positive $C^{1,1}$ densities, we prove that the iteration has local geometric convergence in $C^{2,α}$ on smooth connected Riemannian domains. The iteration is then discretized using a spectral Galerkin method, with local convergence proved for the Fourier-Jacobi scheme on spherical caps. Optical numerical experiments support these estimates and demonstrate useful imaging performance beyond the local convergence theory.

papers.title: Statistical mechanics and hierarchy of learnability in quantum codes: From generalized symmetries to non-Abelian topological orders
papers.abstract: Local weak measurements provide noisy information about observables encoded in a quantum code. We formulate the corresponding Bayesian inference problem for a broad class of topological stabilizer codes by mapping it to classical spin models with generalized symmetries. When the wavefunction deformation and Gaussian measurement strengths coincide, the replicated model acquires an enlarged symmetry. We use this symmetry to derive exact identities among correlators averaged over measurement records that quantify the learnability of nonlocal observables associated with fractionalized excitations. Together with correlation inequalities in the associated clean ferromagnetic models, these identities establish hierarchies of learnability: if two observables remain learnable at long distances, their product must also remain learnable. We demonstrate these relations in the rank-2 toric code and the X-cube model, whose classical descriptions exhibit modulated and subsystem symmetries, respectively. We further extend the analysis to finite group quantum double models, including non-Abelian ones. We derive exact relations between learnability and correlations in the corresponding classical models, and show that the representation structure and fusion rules of anyons impose further constraints under suitable positivity conditions. These results constrain which types of nonlocal information can be learned simultaneously, providing a guide to learning phase diagrams in quantum codes under local weak measurements.

papers.title: Eco-MP: Ecological Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control with Ecological Driving
papers.abstract: Max-pressure (MP) traffic signal control provides a decentralized mechanism for urban networks, but conventional pressure states do not directly capture the propulsion burden generated by signal-induced stop-and-go traffic. Eco-driving, by contrast, typically relies on prespecified signal information and optimizes vehicle trajectories separately from the feedback among vehicle motion, traffic states, and signal decisions. This paper develops Ecological Max-Pressure (Eco-MP), a closed-loop framework that integrates ecological MP signal control with MP-adaptive ecological driving. At the signal layer, connected-vehicle observations are aggregated into a common movement state based on cumulative positive propulsion work, and the resulting upstream--downstream ecological pressure determines phase selection in mixed petrol and electric traffic. At the vehicle layer, a rolling signal interface translates the evolving Eco-MP process into near-term signal information, while each connected and automated vehicle solves a powertrain-independent finite-horizon trajectory problem subject to vehicle-dynamic, car-following, and signal-compliance constraints to reduce unnecessary stopping and acceleration effort. Under full-state information, a finite-storage Lyapunov analysis establishes strong stability for admissible demands satisfying a strict supportability condition and extends the result to the coupled signal--vehicle system. When ecological driving enlarges the admissible-flow sets, the coupled admissible demand region contains the signal-only region. Microscopic experiments on an Amsterdam arterial corridor show that, relative to queue-based MP, Eco-MP reduces mean positive propulsion work by 5.2%, vehicle delay by 20.8%, and stopping time by 39.0%. With only 15% of vehicles directly controlled, ecological driving further reduces positive propulsion work by 4.2% and stopping time by 19.6%......

papers.title: Fluctuations in Environmental Resource Availability Alter the Oscillatory Tragedy of the Commons
papers.abstract: Environmental noise in real-world complex systems--including fluctuations in temperature, humidity, and related environmental conditions--inevitably modulates individual metabolic capacity and, consequently, the efficiency of public-resource utilization. Yet conventional evolutionary game models incorporating environmental feedback treat resource dynamics deterministically. Here, we incorporate stochastic fluctuations into a noise-corrected replicator-dynamics framework. Theoretical analysis and stochastic birth-death simulations yield a counterintuitive result: moderate environmental noise stabilizes, rather than destabilizes, the interior fixed point across diverse payoff landscapes, while suppressing or eliminating catastrophic oscillations. These findings reframe environmental variability not merely as a perturbation but as a mechanism that fosters strategy coexistence and sustainable resource use in complex social and ecological systems.

papers.title: Neural Stochastic Forecasting for Lateral Molecular Diffusion Simulations
papers.abstract: Predicting the long-time diffusion of membrane proteins is challenging because molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are computationally expensive, while experimental single-particle tracking is often limited by finite observation times. Here, we introduce a neural stochastic (NS) model for forecasting the collective diffusion of membrane proteins from coarse-grained MD trajectories. The model combines a transformer-based representation of protein configurations, recurrent networks operating at multiple temporal scales, and a stochastic latent process with learned memory. A cross-attention decoder then generates correlated protein displacements while accounting for the instantaneous system geometry and periodic boundary conditions. We evaluate the model in two membrane systems: seven interacting PIEZO channels and a mixed system containing seven PIEZO and ten TREK channels. For the seven PIEZO system, the NS model reproduces the anomalous diffusion exponent measured in MD simulations $α\sim 1$, substantially improving on a previously developed variational autoregressive model that exhibits superdiffusive behavior. The model also generates trajectories extending to 40,000 frames and captures the distinct diffusion characteristics of PIEZO and TREK populations in the mixed system. Comparisons of time-averaged mean-square displacements, Van Hove displacement distributions, and non-Gaussian parameters show that the model preserves key statistical features of the simulated dynamics. These results establish neural stochastic modeling as a promising approach for generating long trajectories of multi-protein membrane diffusion and extending the statistical analysis of molecular dynamics simulations.

papers.title: Selective Prediction Intervals: Jointly Learning to Predict, Bound, and Abstain
papers.abstract: Many high-stakes regression decisions ask three things of a model at once: a point estimate to act on, an interval that bounds the risk of acting, and the option to abstain when neither can be trusted. Deep learning provides these in isolation: prediction-interval methods return an interval, and at best a value estimate inside it, for every input, while selective-prediction methods learn when to abstain, but only for point predictions and with no statement of how far the truth may lie from the estimate. We introduce SelPI, which trains interval, value and abstention heads jointly under a single loss with an explicit acceptance-rate budget. A natural objection is that interval width already tells us when to abstain. We show that it does not: across 18 tabular benchmarks, width predicts large point errors well (AUROC 0.72) but is anti-correlated with interval misses (AUROC 0.38), so abstaining on wide intervals discards precisely the inputs the interval got right. SelPI therefore selects with two gates, one trained on the interval loss and one on the value loss, coupled by a Fr'echet penalty that ties their separate budgets to the joint acceptance rate they deliver. With the base predictor held fixed, the learned gate beats width thresholding on a proper interval score on all 18 tabular datasets, closing a median 87% of the gap to an oracle selector, and it also beats selection by deep-ensemble disagreement on every dataset. The advantage grows with the heteroscedasticity of the task, and we report the settings in which it disappears.

papers.title: Regret Bounds for Market Making with Persistent Orders
papers.abstract: We study adversarial market making with orders that remain active until execution. The maker operates on two markets: a primary market where orders are made and a secondary market where the resulting positions are hedged. In each round, the maker posts a quote on the primary market before observing both primary and secondary market prices. An order executes when the primary price reaches its quote, and the resulting position is immediately offset at the secondary price. When both price sequences are chosen by an adversary over $T$ rounds, we give a simple deterministic policy with regret of order $\log T$ against the best fixed quote (static comparator) and $\sqrt T$ against the best quote for each submission date (dynamic comparator), plus two terms measuring exposure to future primary and secondary prices. These rates remain optimal even when both exposure terms vanish and lower bounds show that the exposure terms are necessary. Our policy naturally extends to simultaneous bids and asks, where we show that static and dynamic regret are both characterized (up to constant factors) by the exposures terms (where the primary price exposure $V_T^{\mathrm{two}}$ now accounts for both bids and asks) and a term of order $\sqrt{V_T^{\mathrm{two}}\log T}$. Our policy is simple, efficient and fully parameterless. We extend this setting by demonstrating how natural assumptions on the price processes lead to improved guarantees without changing the policy.

papers.title: DSRS: Teaching MLLMs to Perceive, Reason, and Segment in Complex Driving Scenes
papers.abstract: Existing reasoning segmentation frameworks typically employ multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with broad world knowledge to extract semantics in a human-like manner and generate corresponding segmentation masks. Nevertheless, these frameworks lack the necessary scene-specific awareness. This paper introduces driving scene reasoning segmentation (DSRS), a scene-specific task that requires models to interpret implicit instructions, infer spatial relations, detect potential risks, handle challenging conditions, and comprehend underlying traffic rules, ultimately generating accurate segmentation masks. Meanwhile, we establish a benchmark dataset to facilitate future research on the DSRS task. To pioneer this task, we propose DSRS-Net, a novel architecture with advanced reasoning segmentation capability for automated driving. Specifically, DSRS-Net seamlessly infuses geometric features for deeper reasoning segmentation, without compromising the original multimodal fusion mechanism. This strategy effectively mitigates the modality representation mismatch in MLLMs caused by RGB-only pretraining, while enhancing the integration of geometric, contextual, and linguistic features. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superior performance of DSRS-Net in both driving scene reasoning segmentation and other language-driven segmentation tasks across various public datasets. The source code and dataset will be released upon publication.

papers.title: EEG-based listened-language classification
papers.abstract: From an early age, individuals are continuously exposed to other languages beyond their native tongue; however, the brain s response to these auditory stimuli remains unclear. To investigate this, an experiment was designed to record electroencephalography (EEG) signals from subjects listening to sentences in five different languages, and a specific database was built to enable performing classification tests to distinguish between different languages, and varying levels of language comprehension. By analysing the energy difference between the EEG channels to characterize these signals, different classification tests were conducted using bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (bi-LSTM), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) neural networks. The main objective is the analysis of the brain s response in two different scenarios: when the subject listens to sentences in different languages, and when the subject understands or misunderstands the meaning of a sentence. In tire multi-class classification involving sentences in five different languages, the accuracy attained is 36.37 %. However, in the multi-class classification between understood/understood part of the meaning/didn t understand, the accuracy attained reaches 81.36%. The results obtained for binary classification tests of understand native language or foreign language is 89.09 %. The bi-LSTM neural network achieved the overall best performance. These results demonstrate that the analysis of the EEG signals alone can give information regarding a person s language comprehension level, and can be used for monitoring the learning curve of a new language or to assess comprehension in patients with conditions such as aphasia.

papers.title: A Layered View of LLM Support in Underwater Robotics
papers.abstract: This extended abstract discusses a specific and, in our experience, practically relevant role for large language models (LLMs) in underwater robotics. Our main premise is that, in underwater fielding missions, the immediate difficulty is often not the synthesis of new low-level control laws, but the operation of complex robotic systems under limited communications, partial observability, and expensive field time. In particular, a significant fraction of the effort during sea trials is devoted to fault diagnosis, telemetry interpretation, mission adjustment, and coordination across heterogeneous assets and operators. We argue that LLMs may be useful at this higher operational level, especially when grounded in structured vehicle state, alarms, logs, mission context, and existing planning or validation tools. At the same time, current limitations in grounding, consistency, and causal reasoning make these systems lack the predictability required to guarantee direct control, especially in real-world critical applications, although we do not exclude a future evolution in this direction. This viewpoint suggests a layered architecture in which conventional autonomy remains responsible for control, perception, estimation, and validated mission execution, whereas LLM-based modules serve as an additional support layer for debugging, operator interaction, constrained replanning support, orchestration, and post-mission analysis.

papers.title: Unveiling the Origins of Local Group Galaxies with ELT-SHARP: An Overview of Science Cases
papers.abstract: The $Λ$CDM paradigm successfully describes large-scale cosmic structure, yet tensions possibly persist on galactic and sub-galactic scales. The Milky Way and the Local Universe offer a uniquely accessible laboratory to probe these discrepancies through chemo-dynamical studies of resolved stellar populations. Understanding disk assembly, dynamical heating, and galactoseismology requires wide-field coverage and high-angular-resolution near-infrared spectroscopy capable of penetrating dust-obscured regions and resolving crowded stellar environments. We propose science cases exploiting \textsc{SHARP}, a multi-mode near-infrared spectrograph for Extremely Large Telescopes and future space facilities. Operating over $0.95$--$2.45\,μ$m in a single exposure, \textsc{SHARP} enables efficient access to key stellar and gas tracers across the Galactic bulge, disk, halo, and nearby galaxies. The \textsc{NEXUS} mode provides adaptive-optics-assisted multi-object spectroscopy over a $1.2'\times1.2'$ field with spectral resolutions up to $R\sim17{,}000$, enabling gas and stellar kinematics. Complementarily, the \textsc{VESPER} multi-IFU mode delivers spatially resolved spectroscopy in crowded regions, allowing reconstruction of internal kinematics and stellar population gradients on sub-arcsecond scales. Combined with surveys such as \textit{Gaia}, APOGEE, LAMOST, LSST, 4MOST, and ELT--MOSAIC, this project will map six-dimensional phase-space structures of disk and bulge stars, stellar streams, and nearby disk galaxies (e.g. LMC, SMC). The data will enable investigations of bars, spiral arms, warps, flares, and satellite interactions, providing critical constraints on disk evolution, merger history, and dark matter substructure, and providing stringent tests of $Λ$CDM on the smallest accessible scales.

papers.title: Spin swapping mediated by spin-orbital textures in centrosymmetric multiorbital materials
papers.abstract: Spin swapping converts a primary spin current into a secondary one by interchanging its flow and spin-polarization directions, attributed to spin-orbit scattering or spin-band splitting. Here we uncover a fundamentally distinct route to spin swapping arising from the orbital degree of freedom in the spin pumping to centrosymmetric multiorbital materials \textit{without spin-band splitting}. When the dynamical proximity ferromagnet injects a longitudinal spin current flowing normal to the interface, spin-orbit-entangled orbital textures redirect the injected spins into longitudinal and transverse orbital currents. Their subsequent conversion back to the spin sector generates transverse spin currents with propagation and polarization directions swapped relative to the primary spin current. The swapping efficiency achieves $50\%$ for Ge and Si. Governed by a fourth-rank tensor constrained by crystalline symmetry and without requiring spin-orbit scattering or inversion symmetry breaking, our finding reveals spin-orbital textures as hidden intermediate channels of spin swapping with unexplored material choices and functionalities.

papers.title: Sensing the Variation of Wireless Propagation Environment Based on Channel Knowledge Map
papers.abstract: With the evolution of sixth-generation (6G) wireless systems, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has raised the demand for high-precision environmental perception. To address the limited capability of existing techniques in sensing environmental variations, this work proposes a novel channel knowledge map (CKM)-based sensing framework that enables structural change sensing in the wireless propagation environment. By leveraging historical CKM data and real?time user channel, a mathematical model is formulated to infer the changing reflectors which represents the environment variations. Specifically, we propose the Information Aggregation Based Robust Two-Stage Reflection Point Refinement (IA-TS-RPR) scheme for reflection point (RP) estimation, which first uses block coordinate descent (BCD) and Riemannian manifold optimization (RMO) for initial estimation, then applies virtual base station (VBS) clustering for information aggregation in the sensitive area (SA) to refine the estimation. Furthermore, we propose an Environment Variation Sensing scheme based on the Hausdorff-Nearest Neighbor Criterion and Time-Window Voting (EVS-HC-TWV). Specifically, the Hausdorff distance is used to match each user to its most relevant CKM grid point (GP), and a time-window-based multi-user voting mechanism is further employed to improve robustness against positional deviations. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed IA-TS-RPR scheme maintains sub-meter RP position estimation accuracy under user positioning errors, significantly outperforming the scheme based on time of arrival (ToA), linear minimum mean square error (LMMSE) and least squares (LS). The proposed scheme successfully senses and localizes dynamic reflectors, showing strong generalizability and robustness.

papers.title: Koszul duality and homotopy algebras for operads over quivers
papers.abstract: For a quiver $Q$, we introduce and study $Q$-operads (or operads over $Q$), defined as a special sort of $\mathbf{fc}$-multicategories or virtual double categories, in which the directions of the arrows of $Q$ encode the permitted input orderings. In this higher operadic framework, we construct the bar--cobar adjunction and develop a theory of Koszul duality and homotopy algebras, together with compatibility results under changes of quiver. We treat dg categories and their left modules, right modules, and bimodules as algebras over quiver-operads. We prove that these operads are Koszul and that their resolutions govern the corresponding $A_\infty$ categories and modules. We also categorify Sagave's notion of derived $A_\infty$ algebras and introduce modules over derived $A_\infty$ algebras and categories. Finally, we explain that restriction along a folding of quivers constructs diagonal $A_\infty$ bimodules, while extension along an inclusion of quivers realizes two-sided bar models of derived tensor products.

papers.title: FaCoDiff: Factor-Correlated Diffusion for Multivariate Probabilistic Forecasting
papers.abstract: Multivariate probabilistic forecasting requires modeling cross-variable dependence alongside marginal uncertainty. The challenge is to learn this dependence while controlling marginal noise scales and avoiding dense covariance costs. We propose Factor-Correlated Diffusion (FaCoDiff), which couples a compact conditional statistical estimator with structured denoising. History-conditioned factor loadings use distinct coefficients for forecast-center correction, scale adjustment and noise dependence. Diagonal compensation preserves the estimated marginal noise variances, while low-rank operators enable residual Gaussian likelihood evaluation and noise transport without dense covariance storage or factorization. Factor-derived feature modulation explicitly conditions the denoiser, and a geometry-aware objective accounts for errors after noise transport. The same conditional geometry governs forward perturbations and reverse sampling. Across nine datasets, FaCoDiff achieves the lowest mean variogram score on eight datasets and ranks among the top two on 43 of 54 dataset-metric combinations in the reported comparisons. Matched ablations on Solar and Weather show that factor covariance improves mean Energy and Variogram scores under all four combinations of center and scale correction. Disrupting cross-variable sample pairings while preserving marginal trajectories worsens joint and aggregate scores on both datasets, demonstrating the predictive value of generated cross-variable dependence.

papers.title: BIC-Engineered Silicon Nitride Microring Resonators Enabled by an Etch-Free Laser-Writing Approach
papers.abstract: We report the initial experimental demonstration of a complementary, etch-free approach with fewer fabrication steps, in useful SU-8 ridges written by direct ultraviolet laser lithography on an unpatterned silicon nitride film define waveguides and microring resonators. Because the nitride film is never patterned, scattering at patterned nitride sidewalls does not arise, and the remaining radiative loss is engineered by design. The guided transverse-magnetic mode lies within the continuum of transverse-electric slab modes, and we use bound states in the continuum (BICs) as a design tool to control this radiation. Coupled-mode analysis and full-vectorial simulations show that radiation from the two ridge sidewalls cancels by destructive interference at discrete widths, with a first BIC at 2.25 micron and radiation below 1 dB/cm over a 0.3 micron width window and about 200 nm of bandwidth, and that curvature confines this cancellation to discrete bands of bending radius and width. Laser-written waveguides follow the predicted width dependence of the loss, reaching approximately 1.5 dB/cm near the BIC, where non-radiative loss dominates. A microring designed on a radius-selected BIC band exhibits loaded quality factors up to 1.6 \times 10^4 and, under the over-coupled assignment supported by a coupler model, an intrinsic quality factor of 3.3 \times 10^5. Because radiation is set by a patterned low-index layer on an unetched film, the same approach could be extended to other nanostructures. Optimization of the writing conditions and materials is ongoing.

papers.title: Reasoning-Aware Cross-Modal Association Unlearning in Multimodal Large Reasoning Models
papers.abstract: Multimodal large reasoning models (MLRMs) integrate visual inputs with textual and parametric knowledge, allowing sensitive information to be accessed through cross-modal associations during reasoning. This raises privacy concerns when a visual input should no longer provide access to such information. Machine unlearning can remove this influence without retraining the model from scratch. However, multimodal unlearning methods mainly target samples, concepts, or knowledge content, without separating the knowledge from the cross-modal association through which it is accessed. In reasoning models, target information may disappear from the final answer while remaining in intermediate reasoning, or be replaced by incorrect substitute knowledge. We therefore study cross-modal association unlearning, where the forget target is a designated visual-to-knowledge association: the model should suppress target-bearing behavior under the designated visual context while preserving access to the same knowledge in permitted contexts. We propose Visual-Keyed Counterfactual Rebinding (VKCR), a parameter-efficient framework for cross-modal association editing. VKCR first localizes the edit to a compact association-conditioned parameter subspace. It then reduces support for the designated target at task outputs and counterfactually rebinds the affected reasoning behavior by discouraging target-bearing or unsupported continuations while favoring valid non-sensitive alternatives. We further introduce CLEAR-R and MLLMU-R to evaluate target leakage, hallucinated reassociation, reasoning preservation, and modality-specific utility. Experiments show that VKCR substantially reduces image-conditioned target leakage and hallucinated reassociation, including across heterogeneous task formulations, while preserving non-sensitive visual reasoning and permitted text-only knowledge.

papers.title: CARE-FL: Federated Fine-Tuning of Multimodal LLMs in Resource-Constrained Edge Networks
papers.abstract: Domain-specific adaptation of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in privacy-sensitive edge environments requires federated fine-tuning, yet client selection remains challenging due to heterogeneous multimodal data and modality availability, dynamic system conditions, and evolving client utility during training. We propose Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Federated Fine-Tuning (CARE-FL), a constrained online client-selection framework for federated MLLM Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning. CARE-FL formulates client participation as a sequential decision process and employs Q-value decomposition to address the large combinatorial joint action space through scalable client-level long-term utility estimation. These utilities are learned online using a modified Double Deep Q-Learning (DDQL) scheme, while constraint-aware $ε$-greedy execution selects feasible client subsets under per-round latency and bandwidth constraints. Complementing client selection, an adaptive aggregation mechanism further controls potentially unstable global updates and places greater weight on the previous model when needed. Experiments on the CrisisMMD disaster-response task in emulated heterogeneous wireless edge environments show that CARE-FL achieves higher and more stable test accuracy than the compared client-selection baselines across different system settings, while satisfying the imposed latency and bandwidth constraints.

papers.title: AssameseLM-E2B: An Open-Weight Assamese Language Model for Efficient Consumer-Grade Deployment
papers.abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) excel in high-resource languages, their performance often degrades in low-resource languages due to tokenization inefficiencies, generative instability, and linguistic interference. This paper presents AssameseLM-E2B and its instruction-tuned variant, AssameseLM-E2B-it, a 2-billion-parameter model adapted specifically for low resource Assamese language. Built upon the Gemma-4 architecture, the model incorporates an expanded byte-level BPE vocabulary to reduce tokenization overhead by nearly 500% compared with multilingual 2B--3B baselines. We employ a parameter-efficient Continual Pre-Training (CPT) pipeline with Hybrid LoRA, followed by Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on a balanced, multi-domain dataset to enhance instruction-following and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) capabilities. Evaluation demonstrates a Bits-per-Byte (BPB) score of 0.7488 on FLORES-200, alongside an overall RAG score of 96.7% and 100% refusal accuracy on adversarial unanswerable prompts. Comparative analysis reveals significant limitations in general-purpose baselines, including receptive-productive decoupling, generative degradation on Romanized Assamese, and unintended Bengali script assimilation. These results demonstrate the potential of parameter-efficient adaptation for developing capable, locally deployable language models for low-resource languages under constrained computational resources.

papers.title: GraphSeal: Graph-Augmented Speech Deepfake Detection via Temporal-Spectral Artifact Propagation
papers.abstract: Current speech deepfake detectors treat each utterance as a flat sequence of frames, limiting their ability to capture long-range spectral inconsistencies that span non-adjacent regions of an audio signal. We propose \textbf{GraphSeal}, which constructs a temporal-spectral graph over short speech segments and propagates artifact cues through graph attention layers before a global readout produces the bonafide-vs-spoof decision. Each node in the graph corresponds to a fixed-length segment; edges encode temporal adjacency and spectral similarity, letting the network attend to distant frames that share suspicious spectral patterns. A multi-head graph attention mechanism weights neighboring nodes according to both learned features and edge attributes, and a hierarchical readout aggregates node representations into a single utterance-level embedding for binary classification. GraphSeal is front-end agnostic: it operates on top of any self-supervised or handcrafted feature extractor. On ASVspoof 2019~LA, ASVspoof 2021~LA, ASVspoof~5, and the In-the-Wild dataset, GraphSeal achieves equal error rates of 0.52\%, 2.41\%, 8.17\%, and 5.24\%, respectively, matching or outperforming prior methods that rely on fixed-topology graph networks or purely sequential architectures.

papers.title: Closed-form dyadic Green functions for transversely uniaxial bianisotropic medium with equal magnetoelectric scalars
papers.abstract: A transversely uniaxial bianisotropic medium with equal magnetoelectric scalars was conceived by Weiglhofer in 1994. Using the scalar factorization method, he concluded that the dyadic Green functions of this medium could not be found in closed form. That conclusion is incorrect. The essentials of the derivation are reproduced here, and closed-form expressions are given for all four dyadic Green functions of the unbounded medium, linking the electric and magnetic fields to electric and magnetic source current densities.

papers.title: Network Intrusion Forensic Detection System with Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Digital Chain of Custody
papers.abstract: Deploying an explainable intrusion detection model from a validated laboratory setting into a forensic workflow requires guarantees that benchmarks do not test: that the certified model is the exact artifact applied to a case, that heterogeneous evidence can be classified reliably, and that every step is verifiable. We present MODEXRE, a forensic pipeline that extends a previously validated synthetic-data-trained XGBoost classifier with SHAP explainability (arXiv:2607.00763) into a dual-mode architecture: a Laboratory mode, where models are trained and certified on public and synthetic data, and a Formal mode, where a frozen, hash-verified model performs inference on case evidence under a SHA-256 hash-chained chain of custody. Suricata alerts, CEF firewall logs and packet captures are normalized through OCSF. Four design decisions, each triggered by an observed failure, shaped the architecture: a timestamp leak that inflated Kitsune performance (F1-macro 0.984, 0.662 after correction); a feature-coverage gap that made the 78-feature reference model misclassify a real SSH alert; causal temporal flow aggregation, which raised Kitsune multiclass F1-macro from 0.394 to 0.932; and a certification defect, exposed only by a real packet capture, whereby the pipeline had always trained a binary classifier. After correction, the same capture went from 100% of events flagged as malicious to 87% classified as Normal, with the scanning host identified as Reconnaissance. The default four-class certified model reaches F1-macro = 0.9538 on CICIDS2017-derived evidence; the recertified 18-category model reaches 0.6214, reflecting the real multiclass task. Chain-of-custody verification, model integrity hashing and per-prediction SHAP explanations are reported as measured outcomes.

papers.title: Optimal Error Estimates With Polynomial Dependence on $ε^{-1}$ for Mixed Finite Element Methods of the Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes System
papers.abstract: In this paper, we analyze a first-order convex-splitting mixed finite element scheme for the Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes system, tracking explicitly how the error constants depend on the interface width $ε$. Due to the strong nonlinear coupling inherent in the CHNS system and the singular dependence of the Cahn--Hilliard equation on $ε$, conventional energy-based analyzes often lead to severe dependence of the error constants on $ε^{-1}$, and may even result in exponential growth. Such dependence significantly limits the applicability of the resulting error estimates in the small-interfacial-thickness regime. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a robust parameter error analysis framework with respect to interfacial thickness $ε$. In particular, by introducing $H^{-1}$ approximation properties for the Ritz projection and the Ritz and Stokes quasi-projection operators, together with spectral-type estimates for the discrete perturbed Cahn--Hilliard operator, we effectively control the singular terms arising from the interfacial thickness parameter in the error analysis. Compared with the classical results, which address only the Allen-Cahn or Cahn-Hilliard equation, we adopt a three-term discrete Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality analysis technique and achieve a substantial reduction in the degree of polynomial dependence for the coupled system. Numerical experiments are presented to verify the effectiveness of the theoretical results and to demonstrate the robustness of the method for different parameters of interfacial thickness.

papers.title: One Strategic Woman: Sharp Ranks and a Persistent Core
papers.abstract: In a balanced random stable-marriage market, one fixed woman manipulates men-proposing deferred acceptance to obtain her best attainable partner. We prove that the women's expected average true partner rank is asymptotic to $(\ln n)^2$, improving the previous $O((\ln n)^4)$ bound, while the men's is asymptotic to $n/(2\ln n)$. The men's and women's average ranks, normalized by $n/\ln n$ and $\ln n$, converge jointly in distribution to $(U,U^{-1})$, where $U$ is uniform on $(0,1)$. Under optimal truthful truncation, the span of women's average ranks within the reported stable core, divided by $\ln n$, converges in distribution to $U^{-1}-1$.

papers.title: FireOPS: A Human-Centric Emergency Operations Platform
papers.abstract: Volunteer fire brigades rely on fragmented alerting channels and radio plus paper for situational awareness, hindering a shared common operational picture (COP). FireOPS integrates smartphone alerting, navigation, a live geospatial COP, a district resource-load overview and contextual manuals into a human-centric decision-support surface for commanders and responders, running on an edge + cloud architecture whose dual-channel provides source-level redundancy against failure of either the radio or the provincial server feed; delivery to smartphones still depends on the cloud core and mobile networks. This lessons-learned report presents the design rationale, positions FireOPS within emergency-response information systems research, and reports operational findings from a primary log extract of a major regional flood in 2024 and from the 2025 public app release. A feature-matrix comparison with DIVERA 24/7, blaulichtSMS and the LifeRescue prototype identifies COP, decision support and dual-ingestion redundancy as the main differentiators, and we map the operational gaps observed during the flood to concrete engineering responses, deployed or in active development.

papers.title: A Galois-type Springer theorem for hermitian and generalized quadratic forms
papers.abstract: We prove that anisotropy of nonsingular hermitian and skew-hermitian forms over central simple algebras with involution is preserved under scalar extension to every finite Galois extension of odd degree coprime to the index of the algebra. In characteristic two, the same conclusion holds for generalized quadratic forms over algebras with involution of the first kind, with no nonsingularity assumption on their polar forms. The main tool is an isometry-level descent theorem. For a cyclic extension of odd prime degree, every anisotropic nonsingular form over a division algebra with involution, of rank smaller than the extension degree and with Galois-invariant isometry class, descends to an anisotropic form over the base field. Unlike descent results for Witt classes, this theorem descends the form itself. A bounded-rank reduction, based on injectivity of the Witt-group restriction map, derives the cyclic anisotropy theorem from this descent result; a regularization argument removes the nonsingularity assumption on polar forms in characteristic two, and the Feit-Thompson theorem extends the result to arbitrary finite Galois extensions of odd degree.

papers.title: Hypergraphs with zero uniform Turán density at intermediate levels
papers.abstract: An $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ is uniformly dense with respect to $j$-graphs if, up to a small error, at least a prescribed proportion of the $r$-cliques of every $j$-uniform hypergraph on the same vertex set are edges of $H$. For a forbidden hypergraph $F$, its uniform Turán density at level $j$ is the supremum of these density bounds over arbitrarily large $F$-free hypergraphs with the error tending to zero. For every $r\ge4$ and $1\le j\le r-3$, this paper proves that this Turán density is zero precisely when $F$ admits a vertex ordering in which every $(j+1)$-set shared by two edges occupies the same positions in both edges. This generalizes the zero-density characterizations of Erdős at $j=0$ and of Reiher, Rödl, and Schacht at $j=r-2$, and establishes the latter authors' proposed extension to the remaining nontrivial levels. Consequently, at level $j$, every positive uniform Turán density of a possibly infinite forbidden family is at least $N^{-N}$, where $N=\binom r{j+1}$. The proof combines hypergraph regularity with adjacent exchanges in spreadable random hypergraphs.

papers.title: Efficient Stable Word-RAM Simulation by Population Protocols
papers.abstract: Population protocols model computation by indistinguishable agents interacting in uniformly random pairs, with unary inputs and outputs encoded by state counts. Efficiency requires polylogarithmically many states and polylogarithmic stabilisation time, measured as interactions divided by population size $n$. Stability requires eventual stabilisation to the correct output with probability $1$; silence requires that no agent changes state after stabilisation. Fast stable leader election and majority in leaderless populations require growing state spaces. Despite progress on individual problems, the general computational power of efficient stable protocols remains largely unexplored. We show that it extends beyond semilinear predicates, which characterise constant-state stable computation. We give an efficient, stable, and silent simulation of every $\mathcal{P}$-program: a word-RAM program with running time and number of registers polynomial in $w=Θ(\log n)$. Stabilisation takes polylogarithmic time both in expectation and with high probability. The framework supports general word-oriented computations, including multiple outputs. The construction extends MC$+$ protocols, fast Monte Carlo protocols whose failures are eventually detected as anomalies, and the system of weights. MC$+$ majority comparisons against the weights convert unary inputs into binary registers, with one agent per bit. MC$+$ operations on individual bits emulate RAM instructions, after which outputs are converted back to unary. A detected anomaly triggers a new universal rank-based backup that stabilises correctly and silently. These results open a systematic study of computational power and resource trade-offs, including extensions to external or spatial data.

papers.title: Chiron: Cache Management Empowered by LLM Intelligence for AI Workloads
papers.abstract: AI clusters keep data in remote object stores and rely on local caches to stop GPUs from waiting for data. A cache performs well only when its prefetching and eviction policies match the access pattern, yet these patterns differ across AI workloads and change between phases of one workflow. Existing methods either need code changes, which compromises user transparency, or use low-end heuristics, which cannot follow such changes. Large language models (LLMs) can infer access behavior without user hints, but direct LLM control of cache actions suffers from long reasoning delay, high token cost, and poor decision quality. We present Chiron, a cache system based on advisory switching control. An LLM asynchronously diagnoses the access pattern and recommends a policy. A deterministic harness gates this advice, executes expert-designed policies locally, and returns cache feedback for review. We implement Chiron atop JuiceFS and evaluate it on nine AI workloads. It reduces job completion time by 14.3-41.2% over the best baseline on popular AI workloads.

papers.title: Rohbau3D-Semantics: Dense Semantic and Instance Labels for Point Clouds of Indoor Shell Construction Scenes
papers.abstract: We present the Rohbau3D-Semantics dataset, which adds dense semantic and instance-level labels to laser scans of the previously released Rohbau3D domain data from shell construction sites. The dataset comprises 504 point cloud scenes from 14 survey sites, each captured with a terrestrial laser scanner and stored in a scanner-centered local coordinate system. Unlike point clouds sampled from reconstructed meshes or synthetic building models, the data preserve the characteristic properties of real laser scanning, including non-uniform sampling, measurement artifacts, reflections, and fine geometric detail. Combined with manual labels, expert oversight during pointwise annotation, and full-scene review, this yields a high-quality benchmark for semantic scene understanding in complex built environments. The dataset includes 17 class labels of building components and one background class, along with instance annotations for object-level analysis. In addition to the 3D point clouds, the release also provides scripts for deriving geometrically aligned panoramic and cube-map representations of color, LiDAR reflection intensity, depth, surface normals, semantic labels, and instance labels from the 3D arrays. We describe the acquisition pipeline, annotation protocol, quality-control process, and panorama-generation procedure, and provide benchmark splits and baseline experiments for semantic segmentation. By combining precise terrestrial laser scans, dense annotations, and a wide variety of shell-construction scenes, Rohbau3D-Semantics bridges the gap among synthetic indoor datasets, mesh-derived benchmarks, and smaller construction-specific resources. The dataset is intended to support research on 3D scene understanding, construction-site analytics, and multimodal scene analysis in the built environment. Access and download the full dataset via https://github.com/RauchLukas/rohbau3d

papers.title: Continuous Wideband Multicarrier Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receiver
papers.abstract: This paper investigates continuous wideband orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) reception using an auxiliary (AUX)-assisted five-level Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (RAQR) with a single microwave local oscillator (LO), without requiring additional atomic reception transitions or LO frequency combs. By exploiting Floquet theory, the proposed framework characterizes the dynamic atomic response at finite signal-LO detunings without relying on a quasi-static Taylor expansion around the LO operating point. Specifically, closed-form radio-frequency (RF)-to-electrical conversion expressions are derived from the Lindblad master equation under weak-probe and weak-signal approximations. Building on these expressions, an equivalent multicarrier communication model is established, revealing the inherent frequency selectivity of the atomic response and the resulting subcarrier-dependent amplitude and phase distortions. RAQR-aware zero-forcing (ZF) equalization is developed to enable reliable OFDM reception. Furthermore, analytical results reveal how LO and AUX driving influence the atomic response through dressed-state splitting and energy-level shifts. An upper bound on the LO-referenced half-power span is derived, and an approximately $18$-dB reduction in center-response power per bandwidth doubling is established in the AUX-free strong-LO regime. Simulation results validate the analytical response model and reveal pronounced subcarrier-dependent amplitude and phase variations across over $10$~MHz, highlighting the potential of RAQRs as wideband receiving front ends for future wireless communications.

papers.title: Fano's Inequality and Channel Capacity in the Individual-Sequence Regime
papers.abstract: We derive an individual-sequence analogue of Fano's inequality, replacing entropy by Lempel--Ziv (LZ) complexity and probability of error by empirical error frequency. In the setting considered, an arbitrary encoder maps a message to a channel input sequence $\{x_t\}$, the channel maps the input to an output $\{y_t\}$ in a completely arbitrary manner, and a block finite-state decoder produces an estimate of the channel input from the output. The individual-sequence Fano inequality lower-bounds the empirical symbol-error frequency in terms of the LZ complexity of the channel input conditioned on the channel output. This leads to a channel coding converse: reliable communication at a given rate is possible only if that rate does not exceed the individual-sequence LZ channel capacity, defined as the LZ mutual information maximized over channel inputs and minimized (worst-case) over a noise set. We also prove a matching achievability theorem for the class of \emph{symbol-wise invertible} channels, in which the channel output at each time $t$ is $y_t = f(x_t, v_t)$, $v_t$ being a `noise' variable, and $f(\cdot,v)$ is a bijection for every fixed $v$. This class includes group-additive channels $y_t = x_t \oplus v_t$ studied by Feder and coworkers. For such a channel, any rate below the LZ capacity is achievable with vanishing per-message error frequency, simultaneously for every $v^n$ in a given noise set $\mathcal{N}$, provided $\mathcal{N}$ is closed under block permutations; this condition is satisfied by any noise set that depends on $v^n$ only via its type class with respect to such blocks. The achievability uses a universal decoder that requires no knowledge of the channel and no feedback.

papers.title: Improving Hydrofoil Efficiency Through Simulation-Driven Design Optimization
papers.abstract: Foil windsurfing is a sport in which competitors fine-tune their setup to optimize performance under varying environmental conditions. However, such adjustments are typically guided by intuition. This paper presents a methodology for improving hydrofoil design using computational fluid dynamics. First, structured light scanning was used to obtain the geometry of a conventional hydrofoil. Subsequently, five derived designs have been explored, inspired by advancements in airplane wing design. Following this, a preliminary design was selected, and a design of experiments approach was implemented. Generated simulation data were used to train a machine learning surrogate, which is ultimately used in the multi-objective design optimization. While the surrogate-based approach yielded promising results, it was limited to exploring a restricted set of design parameters. To overcome this constraint, additional improvements were attained through adjoint optimization, demonstrating that comparable performance can be achieved with a distinctly different hydrofoil design. Finally, the conventional design was refined through adjoint optimization. Notably, adjoint optimization yielded a 15% increase in efficiency. The results suggest that both proposed approaches can produce novel hydrofoil designs capable of outperforming the original configuration under specific conditions; however, due to its inherent flexibility, the adjoint approach with realistic constraints offers more freedom in the design exploration process.

papers.title: Can Astra Solve RoboMME without Breaking the Bank?
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation often requires remembering information that is no longer visible, such as an object's location before occlusion or the order of a demonstrated action sequence. A large vision-language planner can read this history, but calling it before every action chunk is slow and costly. We present a three-tier system for the RoboMME benchmark. GPT-6 Astra (System 2) selects a grounded subtask from stored visual history, a $π_{0.5}$ vision-language-action policy (System 1) executes it, and a fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-4B monitor (System 1.5) checks after each action chunk whether the subtask is finished. The instruction is kept until the monitor reports completion or a task-specific event occurs, while the policy keeps acting on new observations. On RoboMME, the system succeeds in 79.13% of episodes with an average of 3.63 Astra calls and 80.84 seconds per episode. This is 34.62 points above the best published non-oracle baseline and 4.95 points below GroundSG+Oracle, which gives the low-level policy ground-truth subgoals.

papers.title: Editing Large Language Models with Geometry-Aware Regularization
papers.abstract: Knowledge editing has become a key technique for updating knowledge in large language models. However, existing methods neglect the geometric structure of the knowledge representation space, leading to two key limitations: they cannot distinguish which pre-trained knowledge should be preferentially preserved (core vs. non-core) nor which new edits are inherently difficult (hard vs. easy). To address this, we propose GEdit, a geometry-aware framework built on a Low-Rank Plus Diagonal (LR+D) factor model that captures the intrinsic low-rank structure of Transformer FFN hidden representations. GEdit features two complementary mechanisms. First, the low-rank regularization applies targeted protection on a low-rank core knowledge subspace. Second, the adaptive regularization dynamically adjusts the regularization strength based on each edit request's editability: relaxing constraints for hard edits to ensure success, and tightening them for easy edits to better preserve pretrained knowledge. Extensive experiments on GPT2-XL, GPT-J, and LLaMA-3-8B under large-scale editing scenarios, including both mini-batch and fully sequential editing settings with up to 10,000 continuous updates, show that GEdit consistently and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both editing success and knowledge preservation.

papers.title: Mobility-Aware Mobile Edge Computing for Energy-Balanced Data Collection in IoT-Enabled Underwater Sensor Networks
papers.abstract: Underwater wireless sensor networks (UWSNs) face critical challenges in energy imbalance, connectivity, and data collection due to harsh environments. To address these issues, this paper focuses on the problem is how to achieve energy-balanced data collection in IoT-enabled UWSNs with a mobility-aware mobile edge computing (MEC), named MECEBDC. Unlike existing approaches, the proposed scheme jointly optimizes energy-aware clustering, cluster head selection, and AUV-assisted data collection. Furthermore, we design a novel metaheuristic-based AUV routing algorithm that incorporates realistic underwater mobility dynamics, explicitly considering gravitational pressure and buoyancy forces acting on the AUV. By leveraging the computing, storage, and mobility capabilities of MEC-enabled AUVs, the proposed approach enables efficient trajectory planning and adaptive data gathering in a stable 3D underwater environment. Extensive simulations and theoretical analysis demonstrate that the proposed method significantly reduces node energy consumption, improves data collection efficiency, and prolongs network lifetime compared with existing schemes, making it well suited for long-term underwater IoT applications.

papers.title: Linear maps of $C^*$-algebras preserving norm parallelism
papers.abstract: Two elements $a,b$ in a normed space are parallel if $\|a+γb\|=\|a\|+\|b\|$ for some $|γ|=1$; they form a triangle equality attaining (TEA) pair if $\|a+b\|=\|a\|+\|b\|$. For finite-dimensional complex $C^*$-algebras other than $\mathbf M_2(\mathbb C)$ and $\mathbb C\oplus_\infty\mathbb C$, bijective linear maps on these algebras preserving parallel or TEA pairs are scalar multiples of isometries. For unital abelian algebras with spectra containing at least three points, preservation in both directions gives the same conclusion. We obtain corresponding results for type I factors, simple type I $C^*$-algebras, and unitarily invariant operator spaces under additional continuity and finite-rank hypotheses. All results for $C(X)$ and $B(H,K)$ hold over both real and complex fields.

papers.title: ProGram: A Grammar for Progressive Computation Pipelines
papers.abstract: Progressive Visual Analytics (PVA) systems have demonstrated the effectiveness of time-bounded, incremental computation for exploring large-scale data. However, our survey reveals that existing PVA implementations are often difficult to reuse and extend, as their progressive behaviors are typically realized through ad hoc, hard-coded mechanisms distributed across servers and clients. To address this limitation, we present ProGram, a grammar for progressive computation pipelines. Informed by a comprehensive analysis of prior concepts and design practices in existing PVA systems, ProGram is designed to support core progressive features while reducing implementation burden. Furthermore, we extend the design space by introducing novel mechanisms, such as lockstepping, forking, and temporary prioritization, to better support diverse usage scenarios. Finally, we demonstrate the expressiveness and coverage of ProGram by reproducing and extending existing progressive visualization systems, presenting a gallery of progressive computation pipelines, and discussing the grammar coverage.

papers.title: A minimal E/I circuit model explains differential recovery from amblyopia under TTX and reverse occlusion
papers.abstract: Recovery from amblyopia beyond the critical period remains a major challenge in visual neuroscience. Experimental studies show that transient inactivation of the fellow eye with tetrodotoxin (TTX) produces stronger and more persistent recovery than reverse occlusion (RO), despite both interventions reducing competition from the fellow eye. The circuit mechanisms underlying this difference remain unclear. We develop a minimal cortical circuit model combining excitatory-inhibitory population dynamics, BCM-like metaplasticity, homeostatic regulation, and eye-specific synaptic plasticity. Monocular deprivation drives the network into an amblyopic operating regime with reduced excitatory activity and fellow-eye dominance. Phase-plane and operating-regime analyses show that TTX and RO subsequently place the circuit in distinct dynamical states. TTX lowers inhibitory activity while maintaining excitatory activity above the BCM modification threshold, creating a larger plasticity-permissive regime than RO. These differences produce stronger recovery of amblyopic-eye responsiveness and greater correction of ocular dominance under TTX. A local robustness analysis across 300 perturbed parameter sets shows that the TTX advantage is not dependent on a narrowly tuned parameter choice. These results provide a mechanistic account of the differential efficacy of fellow-eye inactivation and suggest that recovery from sensory deprivation depends not only on changes in sensory input, but also on the dynamical operating regime of the cortical circuit.

papers.title: Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU): Selection of active galactic nuclei and star-formation emission with machine-learning techniques
papers.abstract: Sources detected by recent large-area radio surveys require robust classification and characterisation. The Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) is a prime example of machine-learning (ML) techniques efficiently enriching existing catalogues with classifications and derived physical properties that would be impractical to obtain from spectroscopy or colour selection alone. We aim to build a labelled sample of sources in the EMU pilot survey (EMU-PS, at 944 MHz, with rms ~ 30 uJy/beam over 270 deg2 in the southern sky) classified as being dominated by active galactic nuclei (AGNs) or non-AGN processes including star-formation. We will then use this sample to examine radio properties and redshift-dependent trends. We applied a pre-trained multi-stage ML pipeline to optical-to-infrared photometry of EMU-PS sources to derive classifications and photometric redshifts, which we used to compute additional radio properties, including luminosities. We increase the known number of AGNs and non-AGNs in the EMU-PS by more than a factor of 15 (recall 96 %) up to z ~ 5, and by nearly a factor of 100 (recall 94 %) for z > 1, respectively. In extrapolating these numbers for the full EMU survey, we expect to recover more than 3.4 million AGN candidates. A non-negligible low-redshift subsample of selected non-AGNs shows radio luminosities in excess of those expected from star formation alone, revealing detachment between photometric and radio classification. Radio-derived properties show expected trends for luminosities and a lack of evolution for in-band (800-1088 MHz) spectral indices. The ML-based pipeline provides a scalable way to produce large catalogues for the ongoing EMU survey and future Square Kilometre Array observations and reveals that multi-wavelength analysis can uncover radio populations and trends often missed by colour cuts or spectroscopy alone.

papers.title: GPUMAP: GPU-Accelerated Progressive Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection
papers.abstract: Dimensionality reduction (DR) techniques are fundamental to the analysis of high-dimensional data, yet their substantial computational cost limits their use in interactive settings. To address this limitation, we present GPU-accelerated Progressive Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (GPUMAP), an efficient progressive DR algorithm designed for interactive use. We identify three atomic operations within UMAP and restructure them into a progressive pipeline. As part of this adaptation, we introduce modifications to UMAP, including operation queues, instance-wise local join, and scheduling strategies. We further accelerate computation by leveraging GPU parallelism, enabling interactive analysis of million-scale datasets on commodity GPU hardware. Finally, we employ our implementation to systematically study the behavior of progressive DR, investigating how projections evolve over time relative to the ground-truth projection and how biased data streams influence the quality and stability of the resulting projections.

papers.title: Data-Driven Likelihood-Ratio Construction for Radar Detection via Bernstein Induction Operators
papers.abstract: Accurate likelihood-ratio (LR) construction is challenging when clutter statistics are unknown. Prespecified clutter models may not adequately describe the observed data, and evaluating target-present densities may require computationally expensive marginalization. This paper proposes a data-driven LR construction framework based on a Bernstein polynomial model (BPM) and a Bernstein induction operator (BIO). The BPM weights are estimated from clutter-only samples, whereas the target-induced responses of the Bernstein basis densities are approximated offline in the same basis to construct column-stochastic matrices. These matrices map clutter-density weights to target-present density weights at specified signal-to-clutter ratios (SCRs), and mixtures of the matrices account for target fluctuations. For a fixed target model and basis representation, the matrix library is independent of the clutter-density weights and can be reused across clutter distributions. The resulting LR construction avoids repeated online evaluation of the physical-induction integrals. Simulations under analytical clutter models show close agreement with the reference LRs and detection probabilities, with lower online computation times in the non-Gaussian cases considered. Experiments using synthetic target echoes embedded in measured sea clutter further show improved detection probabilities relative to the evaluated baselines in the weak-target regime.

papers.title: Rational Torsion and Ramification Constraints on Odd Superelliptic Jacobians
papers.abstract: Let C: y^d = f(x) be a smooth projective superelliptic curve over Q, where d >= 3 is odd, f(x) in Q[x] is separable of degree n >= 3, and gcd(d,n) = 1. Let J = Jac(C) be its Jacobian. We study the rational torsion subgroup J(Q)_tors through the interaction of ramification geometry, Galois actions, reduction at primes of good reduction, and the geometry of divisors. First, we describe the subgroup R_d contained in J[d] generated by the ramification-point differences and determine its Galois-invariant subgroup explicitly in terms of the sizes of the Galois orbits of the roots of f. This yields a precise description of the rational d-torsion classes arising from ramification, without assuming that they account for all of J(Q)[d]. Second, we establish criteria based on the orders of reduced Jacobians that can prove the vanishing of the full rational torsion subgroup. Finally, we derive geometric constraints on divisor classes represented by effective divisors of degree smaller than the genus, including a restriction arising when distinct effective divisors represent the same class. Explicit examples illustrate how the Galois-theoretic and reduction-theoretic methods can be combined to study rational torsion on odd superelliptic Jacobians.

papers.title: Cross-Asset Knowledge Transfer for Early Fault Detection of Data-Scarce Assets Without Target Fault Data
papers.abstract: Reliability management of industrial fleets depends on early fault warnings, yet lifecycle data across similar assets are highly imbalanced. A few assets accumulate run-to-failure histories, while newly installed or rarely failing assets provide only normal-condition data. This paper asks how diagnostic knowledge can be transferred from a data-rich source asset to a data-scarce target asset when no fault data have been observed on the target. We formulate cross-asset early fault detection as a zero-shot domain adaptation problem, in which zero-shot refers to the absence of target fault samples, and propose a framework that requires only normal data from the target. The framework comprises (1) a statistical process control step that labels the source asset run-to-failure data with an exponentially weighted moving average chart, reducing manual annotation to verifying flagged segments, (2) an Adapted Domain-Adversarial Neural Network (ADANN) that combines domain-adversarial training and a Maximum Mean Discrepancy penalty with an Adapted Classification-Domain (ACD) loss, which anchors the classifier normal region to the target own normal data, and (3) an ahead-of-time labeling scheme with a prediction horizon that targets incipient faults. Under an exact-classification assumption, a theoretical analysis characterizes the domain-adversarial term for a normal-only target and the alignment state in which source fault features remain separated from target normal features. On a public run-to-failure bearing dataset, ADANN attains the highest mean F1-score among four transfer baselines, with a nominally significant precision gain over the strongest baseline, and its robustness is examined under synthetic noise.

papers.title: Annotator-Free Object Detection via Foundation Model Collaboration
